quantitative_stability_lemma.precise_statement: Fix one finite positive probability space (X,mu), two actual symmetric nonnegative Markov kernels T_0,T relative to mu, and six fixed positive integers n_e. Set N=sum_e n_e, M_0=||T_0||_infinity and epsilon=||T-T_0||_infinity. Let F_n(T)=E_mu^4 product_(e=vw in K4)(T^(2n_e))(x_v,x_w). Then |F_n(T)-F_n(T_0)|<=2N epsilon(M_0+epsilon)^5. The kernel infinity norm means maximum ABSOLUTE ENTRY of the kernel relative to mu, not maximum entry of the row-transition matrix.
proof: For any nonnegative Markov kernel Q relative to mu, left composition averages a kernel row with nonnegative coefficients summing1. Symmetry also gives column averages summing1, so right composition is an infinity-norm contraction. The identity endpoints act exactly as identity; their kernels 1_(x=y)/mu_y create no norm factor in composition.

The telescoping identity T^s-T_0^s=sum_(j=0)^(s-1) T^j(T-T_0)T_0^(s-1-j) therefore gives ||T^s-T_0^s||_infinity<=s epsilon for every positive integer s. It uses the same original mu on both sides and requires no spectral simplicity, irreducibility or positive lower bound on entries.
Markov averaging also gives ||T^s||_infinity<=||T||_infinity<=M_0+epsilon and ||T_0^s||_infinity<=M_0 for every s>=1. In particular all six powered factors are nonnegative and bounded by M_0+epsilon.

Telescope the product of six scalar factors, changing them one at a time. Each replacement contributes at most 2n_e epsilon(M_0+epsilon)^5 pointwise in absolute value. Integrate over the original probability mu^4 and sum the six bounds. This proves the stated inequality.
quantitative_stability_lemma.meaning: This is an elementary finite-kernel Lipschitz estimate. It is not a new universal lower bound by itself and is not a novelty or B-level claim.

two_level_open_neighborhood_corollary.precise_base: On the same original (X,mu), |X|>=2, let actual T_0 be symmetric nonnegative Markov and suppose A_0=T_0^2=yI+(1-y)Pi+(x-y)P, where P is a real centered orthogonal projection, 0<=y<=x<=1, and A_0 is not Pi. The entire centered spectrum has this form, not two positive values plus an additional unrepresented zero complement.
two_level_open_neighborhood_corollary.buffer_y_positive: If y>0, define delta_0=y^N[sum_x mu_x^(-2)-1]>0. In the prior common-one-S convex decomposition of each A_0^n, the all-I assignment has weight y^N. Every elementary assignment has density>=1, while the all-I density is sum_x mu_x^(-2). Hence F_n(T_0)>=1+delta_0.
two_level_open_neighborhood_corollary.buffer_y_zero: If y=0, non-IID means x>0 and rank(P)=d>0. Define delta_0=x^(N-6)[(1+d x^3)^2-1]>0. Here A_0=Pi+xP and A_0^n=(1-x^(n-1))Pi+x^(n-1)A_0. The all-A_0 assignment has weight x^(N-6); the existing homogeneous K4 bound is t(K4,A_0)>=[Tr A_0^3]^2=(1+d x^3)^2. All other assignments have density>=1. Thus the displayed buffer follows. Since N>=6 and x>0, no negative power or ambiguous0^0 occurs.
two_level_open_neighborhood_corollary.explicit_radius: Let R=min(1,delta_0/[4N(M_0+1)^5]). Every actual symmetric nonnegative Markov T on the SAME original mu with ||T-T_0||_infinity<=R satisfies F_n(T)>=1+delta_0/2. Indeed epsilon<=1 implies the stability error<=2N epsilon(M_0+1)^5<=delta_0/2.
two_level_open_neighborhood_corollary.scope: The radius depends on the finite host and the fixed tuple. Perturbations may split the centered eigenspaces into three or more distinct bands; no two-level spectral assumption is imposed on T itself. This is a quantitative local extension around a proved host class, not a uniform all-host or all-tuples theorem. A_0=Pi and the singleton case are excluded from the positive-buffer assertion; the singleton density is trivially1.

explicit_three_band_actual_host.purpose: An exact illustration that the local robustness corollary admits three interacting spectral levels outside several explicitly checked sufficient classes. It is not a target counterexample, a broad numerical test or a novelty claim.
explicit_three_band_actual_host.original_space: Uniform mu=1/20 on20states. Let T_0=(Pi+I)/2 as an actual kernel: its diagonal entries are21/2 and its off-diagonal entries are1/2. Then A_0=T_0^2=(3/4)Pi+(1/4)I.
explicit_three_band_actual_host.tuple: Take k=3,r=u=l=h=1, giving six exponents(3,2,1,1,1,1) and N=9. This avoids the three listed reflected faces k=r,u=l; k=r+h,u=l; and k=u,r=l.
explicit_three_band_actual_host.radius: delta_0=(20^3-1)/4^9=7999/262144. Put R=delta_0/[36*(23/2)^5], which is strictly between0and1. This is the explicit stability radius with M_0=21/2; no decimal or approximate inequality is used.
explicit_three_band_actual_host.actual_perturbation: Let v=(sqrt(10),-sqrt(10),0,...,0) and w=(0,0,sqrt(10),-sqrt(10),0,...,0). They are centered orthonormal under original mu. Put T=T_0+(R/20)v tensor v+(R/40)w tensor w. The perturbation infinity norm is exactly R/2. All entries of T remain strictly positive: only entries(1,2),(2,1) decrease by R/2, and entries(3,4),(4,3) decrease by R/4, from the positive baseline1/2. Centering gives all weighted row means1, and symmetry is exact.
explicit_three_band_actual_host.bounded_host: The maximum entry of T is21/2+R/2, attained on the first two diagonal states. Set W=T/(21/2+R/2); then0<W<=1, its weighted row mean is p=(21/2+R/2)^(-1), and T=W/p is the actual root relative to original mu.
explicit_three_band_actual_host.three_centered_bands: The centered eigenvalues of T are1/2+R/20 on v,1/2+R/40 on w, and1/2 on the17-dimensional remaining centered subspace. Their squares give three distinct positive centered bands of A=T^2. The base is two-level only; the perturbed host is not.
explicit_three_band_actual_host.checked_thresholds_fail: p<1/4, so the d=0,h=1 density threshold gamma=1/4 fails. At state5, T^2 has diagonal kernel entry23/4, unchanged by the two localized spectral perturbations. Thus max K_1>=23/4, and gamma max K_1>=23/16>1: the existing mixing certificate also fails at this tuple.
explicit_three_band_actual_host.not_hierarchical: The unique highest centered eigenspace is span(v). If T or A were a nonnegative mixture of nested conditional-expectation projections, constants plus that highest eigenspace would be the range of a conditional-expectation projection, even with repeated partition levels and zero mixture weights. Its kernel would be Pi+v tensor v, whose entry(1,2) is1-10=-9. A conditional-expectation kernel is nonnegative, a contradiction.
explicit_three_band_actual_host.conclusion: The local stability theorem proves F_n(T)>=1+delta_0/2. This example is outside the checked two-level, nested hierarchy, density/mixing and listed reflection cases. No claim is made that it lies outside every previous sufficient class; in particular an exhaustive tensor-class classification is not part of this illustration.

existing_hierarchy_audit.actual_source: research-note.tex existing Hierarchical common powers proposition, lines511-558 at the read source above.
existing_hierarchy_audit.verdict: PASS: the existing recursive proof retains conditional original measures, cell-mass exponent v-m, connected m>=v-1, and power coefficients q_j^s-q_(j+1)^s. Unequal cell masses, zero mixture weights and reducible hosts are handled correctly.
existing_hierarchy_audit.shorter_check: For elementary nested conditional-expectation edge kernels, choose a maximum-level spanning forest. Every omitted edge's level is at most each level on its retained forest path. By nesting, that edge's equality constraint follows on the forest support; its factor1/mu(cell)>=1. Pointwise the full product is at least the forest product, whose Markov-kernel density is exactly1. This gives another audit proof, not new coverage.
existing_hierarchy_audit.boundary: Nested actual conditional-expectation partitions are essential to this argument. General PSD cutoffs may have negative entries; merely commuting kernels or projections do not satisfy the constraint implication. Tensor-product closures are also already in the public note and are not being relabeled new.

remaining_compensation_obligation.full_expansion: F=1+four nonnegative centered triangle terms+three nonnegative centered four-cycle terms+six nonnegative centered diamond terms+the potentially negative full six-centered term Q. The coefficients are constrained by actual multiplication moments on the original probability space and by one actual Markov root.
remaining_compensation_obligation.not_a_shortcut: Q>=-(triangles+cycles+diamonds) is exactly equivalent to F>=1 and is not recorded as a newly solved lemma. Bounding |Q| by a fixed dimension-free linear combination of proper terms is already refuted on flat hosts with positive Q. Individual actual spectral source coefficients can be negative. A different PSD nonnegative Markov kernel at each edge, even with pairwise commutation, is already refuted.
remaining_compensation_obligation.prefix_route: For the ac expansion, group complete positive centered eigenspaces and retain the uncentered diamond surplus R_0>=1. Abel summation reduces a sufficient route to R_0+S_j>=1 for each proper full spectral prefix. Neither bare prefix positivity nor this slack-retaining condition is established on arbitrary hosts. The general criterion cannot be supplied by an arbitrary-vector weighted PSD assertion, which is false even on actual hosts.
remaining_compensation_obligation.commutator_route: The exact prefix decomposition has a nonnegative Gram anchor plus distinct-band double-commutator terms. The desired domination requires actual source/multiplication constraints; no general bound was obtained in this round. Loewner ordering of common powers does not on its own justify density monotonicity or a positive triple-PSD trace.
remaining_compensation_obligation.unresolved_region: Arbitrary actual finite weighted hosts with genuinely interacting centered spectra, outside the already proved density/mixing, low-state, flat/two-level, hierarchy/tensor and reflected cases and their local neighborhoods. There is no demonstrated admissible counterexample here.
